title: Council appointments to committees and boards
subtitle: Committee chairs, a larger library board, a council seat on Heritage Guelph, and The Elliott's management committee.
overview: Council met on December 6, 2022, and spent most of the evening on appointments for the 2022-2026 term. After a closed session on public appointments, Council approved in open session the residents named to advisory committees, local boards and commissions {{vote:m2}}. Staff were also directed to keep recruiting for remaining vacancies, and the Guelph Sports Hall of Fame Board of Directors was dissolved at its own request.

Council filled the chair and vice-chair roles for its Committee of the Whole bodies, for example Councillor Downer as Public Services chair {{vote:m9}}. It also named councillors to outside boards, including the Grand River Conservation Authority {{vote:m16}}, the Police Services Board {{vote:m17}} and the public health board {{vote:m21}}.

Two structural changes affect how Council connects with local bodies. The library board will have 3 council members and 10 public members {{vote:m18}}. Council also set aside rules to add a non-voting councillor to Heritage Guelph {{vote:m23}}. The Committee of Management for The Elliott was reshaped {{vote:m14}}. These changes give Council more direct involvement in these bodies.

decisions.detail: Council appointed and reappointed residents to advisory committees, local boards and commissions, directed further recruitment for vacancies, and dissolved the Guelph Sports Hall of Fame Board of Directors at its request.
Council reappointed four members and appointed five new members to Heritage Guelph.
The Guelph Public Library Board of Directors will now have 10 public members and 3 City Council members.
Councillor Downer was appointed to Heritage Guelph as a non-voting member for a term ending November 2024.
Council waived the appointment policy and Heritage Guelph terms of reference provisions so a non-voting councillor could be appointed.
The committee's composition was amended to include the service area vice-chairs, the Public Services chair and Council's appointee to The Elliott board.
Councillor Downer was appointed chair of the Committee of the Whole Public Services for a term ending November 15, 2024.
Mayor Guthrie and Councillor Allt were appointed to the Guelph Police Services Board for a term ending November 15, 2026.

debate: Before the closed session, a councillor declared a conflict of interest because a family member had applied. The Mayor said that councillor would not take part in the related discussion.

Two councillors seeking the Corporate Services vice-chair role each described their background. One pointed to project management and technology experience. The other pointed to public-sector education, human resources, and audit and budget experience.

A councillor asked what happens if one person is vice-chair of two committees, since vice-chairs sit on The Elliott's Committee of Management. Staff said Council could amend the motion to appoint another councillor if needed.

The mover of the library board change said more councillors would improve communication between the board and Council. They also said a larger new main branch under the Baker Street redevelopment would raise the operating budget, and that councillors on the board could influence the budget earlier. The mover said they had consulted the library's executive director and board chair.

Supporting a councillor seat on Heritage Guelph, a councillor cited a past facilitation report that recommended it, and peer cities with one or two councillors on their heritage committees. They also said provincial changes under Bill 23 made a link to Council timely.
